_comment: PINNED host-path vectors for the content-bridge mirror model (planning doc 119).
The web app holds a byte-identical COPY of the mirror functions because the two
are separate npm projects and the bridge's Docker build context contains only the
bridge, so a shared module is impossible. This file is the contract between them.
A divergence mounts one path and indexes another, which surfaces as the badly
misleading 'PERMISSION PROBLEM - can't READ content folder'.
`canonical` is normalizeHostPath(input) - the ONE spelling written to bridge.env,
sent on HELLO and stored as a source root's host_path. `mirror` is
hostPathToContainerPath(canonical) - the container side of the bind. null = reject.
The POSIX rows are a REGRESSION FENCE, not decoration: every installed Mac, Linux
and NAS bridge derives its index root through this function, so a changed POSIX
output would silently re-map the entire installed base.

posix.why: Synology NAS - the operator's own prod shape
spaces are preserved on POSIX too
trailing slash is stripped by the canonicalizer

windows.why: the operator's REAL path, exactly as Explorer's 'Copy as path' emits it - quoted, backslashed, and containing a space
same path already forward-slashed (what the wizard's placeholder shows)
CASE STABILITY - Windows treats C: and c: as one drive, so both must land on one mirror or the mount and the index disagree
a drive other than C, with a trailing slash
surrounding whitespace from a sloppy paste

rejected.why: bare drive with no separator is ambiguous on Windows
UNC share - deferred, doc 119 Out of Scope
traversal that would escape the drive root
a colon past the drive letter is not a real Windows path
